nodes.label: MNCs and Modern Globalisation
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Multinational corporations first established in 1920s. Spread worldwide in 1950s-60s. From late 1970s shifted production to low-wage Asian countries. China's opening after 1979 transformed global economy.
nodes.chapter_title: The Making of a Global World

nodes.label: Roman-Indian Trade
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Extensive maritime trade between Rome and India via the Red Sea and Indian Ocean, using monsoon winds. Romans imported pepper, spices, gems, and textiles from India, paying largely in gold. Indian ports like Muziris and Arikamedu show Roman artefacts. The trade declined after the 3rd century CE.

nodes.label: Modernisation
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Process of economic, political, and social transformation involving industrialisation, nation-building, democratisation, and secularisation. In the context of this chapter, it examines how Japan and China followed distinct paths to modernisation in response to Western imperialism. Both sought to strengthen their nations while preserving cultural identity.

nodes.label: National Language Debate
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Fierce debate on whether Hindi in Devanagari script should be national language. North Indian members advocated Hindi. South and non-Hindi speakers opposed. Compromise: Hindi as official language with English continuing for 15 years. States could use regional languages. Anti-Hindi agitation in South continued.
nodes.chapter_title: Framing the Constitution - The Beginning of a New Era

nodes.label: Cricket and Decolonisation
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: After independence, cricket became a means of asserting national identity. West Indian cricketers like Frank Worrell challenged racial discrimination. India's 1983 World Cup victory transformed cricket into national obsession.
nodes.chapter_title: History and Sport: The Story of Cricket

nodes.label: Technology in Cricket
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Cricket adapted slowly to technological change. Unlike other sports, retained much of its original character - pitch length unchanged since 1744. But television, floodlights and limited-overs format transformed the game after 1970s.
nodes.chapter_title: History and Sport: The Story of Cricket
